title: Pilot Lantern: compact canary runbook editor with time-slice previews and cost-delta insights
creator: Aria Chen
description:
Overview:
Design a compact, focused canary runbook editor (Pilot Lantern) embedded within Redwood Console's Rollouts surface. The goal is to let engineers and product owners compose, preview, and rehearse canary steps quickly — with minute-by-minute visual slices, suggested safe defaults, and a live cost-delta estimate for each ramp.

Problems we're solving:
- Current rollout composer is dense and requires too many context switches for small experiments.
- Engineers want a fast way to rehearse rollback actions before committing a canary.
- PMs need affordable insights: what is the incremental cost of a 5% traffic exposure for 24 hours?

Goals & success metrics:
- Author a canary in under 90 seconds (measured in lab tests).
- Decrease average number of clicks to set a four-step canary by 40%.
- Enable users to preview rollback behavior and run a simulated rehearsal without changing live traffic.
- Surface per-step cost delta estimates within the composer; 85% of test participants rate these as "helpful" or "very helpful".

User flows to support:
- Quick-create: pick a source model variant, pick outbound variant(s), choose audience slice, set durations and metrics, and save/launch.
- Time-slice preview: scrub a timeline to see expected latency, SLO risk, and estimated token spend for each minute of the run.
- Rehearsal mode: run an in-console simulation that executes the canary logic against historical telemetry (no live traffic change) and outputs simulated metrics and an auto-generated rollback script.
- Rollback rehearsal: allow engineers to author an emergency revert action that can be rehearsed and then be bound to a quick-apply button during live runs.

Core components proposed:
- Compact header: model/variant selector + primary start/stop actions + small cost summary.
- Timeline lane: minute-by-minute scrubber with brush selection for ranges; each slice shows tiny sparklines for latency, error, and cost.
- Step cards: small editable cards for each step (percent, duration, metric guards, audiences). Cards support inline quick-edit and a more-detailed flyout for advanced config.
- Simulation panel: side panel that runs a simulated execution and outputs step-by-step assertions and a generated rollback playbook.
- Cost-delta lens: a lightweight estimator that shows incremental cost per step and cumulative cost; integrates token cost model and expected throughput.

Accessibility & constraints:
- Keyboard-firstable (timeline scrubbing with arrow keys, step selection).
- Color contrast and non-reliance on color alone for critical state (use icons and labels).
- Must fit within existing Rollouts layout without requiring a full page redesign; target width <= 920px for embedded mode.

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype includes quick-create flow, timeline scrubber, step cards, and simulation panel.
- PM and Eng sign-off on cost estimator assumptions and data sources.
- Usability test with 6 engineers and 4 PMs; qualitative feedback logged and follow-ups captured.

Links & artifacts:
- Prototype (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Pilot-Lantern-Prototype
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/Pilot+Lantern+Runbook+Editor
- Cost model notes (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PilotLantern-Cost-Notes
- Reference PR (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4982

Open questions / risks:
- How accurate are minute-level cost estimates for streaming workloads with variable token rates? Need Eng to validate data feed latency and estimator stability.
- Simulation privacy: is historical telemetry allowed for rehearsal without additional consent? Forward to Legal.
- Rollback playbook execution surface needs careful RBAC gating; coordinate with Security and ENG.
comments: 2026-02-19 - Aria Chen: Drafted initial idea and sketched quick header + step-card interactions. Shared with PM and Eng for initial feasibility check.

2026-02-22 - Marcus Patel (PM): Like the compact approach. Request we add a cost-delta tooltip that explains assumptions (tokens/sec, avg seq len). Also: include a toggle for 'use live pricing' vs 'estimate'.

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor (Eng): Backend feasibility OK. We can surface minute-aggregates from the metrics pipeline; cost estimator will need a small service (ENG-4021) to compute deltas asynchronously.

2026-03-01 - Design critique notes:
- Move the simulation panel to a collapsible rail to preserve width.
- Make rollback rehearsal a two-click flow (record -> preview -> bind).
- Add microcopy for step guard suggestions.
Action: update prototype and include keyboard interactions.

2026-03-05 - Usability lab scheduled: 2026-03-09. Recruit 6 backend engineers + 4 PMs. Test scenarios: quick-create, simulate, rehearse rollback, and inspect cost-delta. Test script uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PilotLantern-UX-Test

2026-03-10 - Usability summary:
- Median author time: 82s (target met).
- Users loved the minute-scrubber but asked for a 'skip to percent' shortcut (jump to 5%, 25%, 50%).
- Cost-delta helpfulness: 75% helpful — need clearer assumptions tooltip.
Next: iterate on scrubber shortcuts, refine estimator tooltip, and draft Eng ticket for estimator service (ENG-5120).
2026-03-11 - Marcus Patel (PM): Please add copy for 'what happens on rollback' in the simulation panel. Also, surface whether a rollback would fail safety checks (preflight).

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Created ENG-5120 to implement the cost-delta service and a simulation harness. Linked PR when ready. Leaving this ticket In Review for final sign-off from Security on telemetry use.
